import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zilber–Pink conjecture

Let $X$ be a mixed Shimura variety or a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and let
$V \subseteq X$ be a subvariety. Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal atypical
subvarieties.

Here an *atypical subvariety* of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of an intersection
$V \cap T$, where $T \subseteq X$ is a special subvariety, such that
$\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$.

This file states the semiabelian case (Zilber's conjecture on intersections with tori and its
extension to semiabelian varieties, independently proposed by Bombieri, Masser and Zannier).
The special subvarieties of a semiabelian variety are the translates of irreducible algebraic
subgroups by torsion points.

The mixed Shimura case (Pink's conjecture) is not stated: mixed Shimura varieties and their
special subvarieties are not available in Mathlib.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Zilber–Pink conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zilber%E2%80%93Pink_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- B. Zilber, *Exponential sums equations and the Schanuel conjecture*, J. London Math. Soc. (2)
  65 (2002), 27–44.
- E. Bombieri, D. Masser, U. Zannier, *Anomalous subvarieties—structure theorems and
  applications*, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2007, no. 19.
- R. Pink, *A common generalization of the conjectures of André-Oort, Manin-Mumford, and
  Mordell-Lang*, preprint (2005).
-/
namespace ZilberPinkConjecture
open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory AlgebraicGeometry
open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj

/-- The base scheme $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$. -/
local notation "𝕊" => Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)

/- We work with a scheme `X` over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$ that is a group scheme over
$\mathbb{C}$, i.e. a group object in the category of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$.
The Zariski topology on `X` is the topology of its underlying space, and the dimension of a
subset is its topological Krull dimension. -/
variable (X : Scheme) [X.Over 𝕊] [GrpObj (X.asOver 𝕊)]

blocks.docstring:
The $\mathbb{C}$-points of `X`: the morphisms from the terminal object of the category
of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$ to `X`, i.e. the sections of the structure
morphism. Since `X` is a group scheme, this is a group (the group $X(\mathbb{C})$).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's Yoneda-style `CategoryTheory.Hom.group` on `X ⟶ G` for group objects (used directly as the group structure); there is no Mathlib notion of k-points of a scheme as a group.
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.Points
justification.why_needed: The ℂ-points X(ℂ) of the group scheme X, as morphisms 𝟙_ (Over (Spec ℂ)) ⟶ X.asOver (Spec ℂ); Mathlib's scoped `Hom.group` instance makes this a group, giving the torsion notion needed for special subvarieties.

blocks.name: Points
blocks.text:
/-- The $\mathbb{C}$-points of `X`: the morphisms from the terminal object of the category
of schemes over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$ to `X`, i.e. the sections of the structure
morphism. Since `X` is a group scheme, this is a group (the group $X(\mathbb{C})$). -/
abbrev Points := 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊

blocks.code: def Points.toPoint (x : Points X) : X := x.left.base (default : 𝕊)
blocks.docstring: The point of the underlying space of `X` corresponding to a $\mathbb{C}$-point.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Scheme.Hom.base` applied to `default : Spec ℂ` (which is what the definition is).
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.Points.toPoint
justification.why_needed: The point of the underlying Zariski space of X determined by a ℂ-point (image of the unique point of Spec ℂ), needed to relate ℂ-points to subsets of X.

blocks.name: Points.toPoint
blocks.text:
/-- The point of the underlying space of `X` corresponding to a $\mathbb{C}$-point. -/
def Points.toPoint (x : Points X) : X := x.left.base (default : 𝕊)

blocks.code:
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Set X) : Prop :=
  IsClosed H ∧ ∃ K : Subgroup (Points X), ∀ x : Points X, x ∈ K ↔ x.toPoint ∈ H
blocks.docstring:
An *algebraic subgroup* of `X`: a Zariski-closed subset `H` of `X` whose
$\mathbb{C}$-points form a subgroup of $X(\mathbb{C})$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has no closed subgroup schemes; `Subgroup (Points X)` is used for the group-theoretic part.
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.IsAlgebraicSubgroup
justification.why_needed: Algebraic subgroups of X: Zariski-closed subsets whose ℂ-points form a subgroup of X(ℂ). Over ℂ (finite type, Jacobson) these are exactly underlying sets of closed subgroup schemes.

blocks.name: IsAlgebraicSubgroup
blocks.text:
/-- An *algebraic subgroup* of `X`: a Zariski-closed subset `H` of `X` whose
$\mathbb{C}$-points form a subgroup of $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Set X) : Prop :=
  IsClosed H ∧ ∃ K : Subgroup (Points X), ∀ x : Points X, x ∈ K ↔ x.toPoint ∈ H

blocks.code:
structure IsSemiabelianVariety : Prop where
  /-- `X` is locally of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `X` is quasi-compact; together with the previous field, `X` is of finite type over
  $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  compactSpace : CompactSpace X
  /-- `X` is connected (equivalently, irreducible). -/
  irreducibleSpace : IrreducibleSpace X
  /-- The group law of `X` is commutative. -/
  isCommMonObj : IsCommMonObj (X.asOver 𝕊)
  /-- Every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of `X` contains a nontrivial torsion
  point. -/
  exists_isOfFinOrder : ∀ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H → IsIrreducible H →
    (∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H) →
    ∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ IsOfFinOrder x ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H
blocks.docstring:
`X` is a *semiabelian variety* over $\mathbb{C}$: a connected commutative algebraic group
over $\mathbb{C}$ (a commutative group scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$
with irreducible underlying space) that is an extension of an abelian variety by an algebraic
torus.

By Chevalley's structure theorem, a connected commutative algebraic group $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$
has a largest connected affine algebraic subgroup $L \cong \mathbb{G}_m^r \times \mathbb{G}_a^s$,
with $X / L$ an abelian variety; $X$ is semiabelian if and only if $s = 0$, i.e. if and only if
$X$ contains no algebraic subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$. Since $\mathbb{G}_a(\mathbb{C})$
is torsion-free, while every nontrivial connected algebraic subgroup of a semiabelian variety is
semiabelian and hence has nontrivial torsion, this is equivalent to the condition used here:
every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of $X$ contains a nontrivial torsion point.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No Mathlib notion of abelian variety, algebraic torus, 𝔾_m or 𝔾_a as group schemes; `IsProper` exists but a quotient/extension-based definition would still need a torus, which is unavailable.
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.IsSemiabelianVariety
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no abelian varieties, tori or semiabelian varieties. Defined as: commutative group scheme of finite type over ℂ (LocallyOfFiniteType + CompactSpace), irreducible, such that every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup contains a nontrivial torsion point. By Chevalley's structure theorem this is equivalent to being an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (⇔ containing no 𝔾_a).

blocks.name: IsSemiabelianVariety
blocks.text:
/-- `X` is a *semiabelian variety* over $\mathbb{C}$: a connected commutative algebraic group
over $\mathbb{C}$ (a commutative group scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$
with irreducible underlying space) that is an extension of an abelian variety by an algebraic
torus.

By Chevalley's structure theorem, a connected commutative algebraic group $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$
has a largest connected affine algebraic subgroup $L \cong \mathbb{G}_m^r \times \mathbb{G}_a^s$,
with $X / L$ an abelian variety; $X$ is semiabelian if and only if $s = 0$, i.e. if and only if
$X$ contains no algebraic subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$. Since $\mathbb{G}_a(\mathbb{C})$
is torsion-free, while every nontrivial connected algebraic subgroup of a semiabelian variety is
semiabelian and hence has nontrivial torsion, this is equivalent to the condition used here:
every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of $X$ contains a nontrivial torsion point. -/
structure IsSemiabelianVariety : Prop where
  /-- `X` is locally of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `X` is quasi-compact; together with the previous field, `X` is of finite type over
  $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  compactSpace : CompactSpace X
  /-- `X` is connected (equivalently, irreducible). -/
  irreducibleSpace : IrreducibleSpace X
  /-- The group law of `X` is commutative. -/
  isCommMonObj : IsCommMonObj (X.asOver 𝕊)
  /-- Every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of `X` contains a nontrivial torsion
  point. -/
  exists_isOfFinOrder : ∀ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H → IsIrreducible H →
    (∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H) →
    ∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ IsOfFinOrder x ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H

blocks.code:
noncomputable def translation (a : Points X) : X.asOver 𝕊 ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊 :=
  lift (toUnit _ ≫ a) (𝟙 _) ≫ μ
blocks.docstring:
Translation $y \mapsto a \cdot y$ by the $\mathbb{C}$-point `a`, as an automorphism of the
$\mathbb{C}$-scheme `X`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No translation morphism for group objects in Mathlib; built from `CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift` and `MonObj.mul`.
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.translation
justification.why_needed: Translation by a ℂ-point a as an automorphism of the ℂ-scheme X (lift (toUnit ≫ a) 𝟙 ≫ μ), used to form the translate a·H of a subgroup. API lemma `comp_translation` checks that y ≫ translation a = a * y in X(ℂ).

blocks.name: translation
blocks.text:
/-- Translation $y \mapsto a \cdot y$ by the $\mathbb{C}$-point `a`, as an automorphism of the
$\mathbb{C}$-scheme `X`. -/
noncomputable def translation (a : Points X) : X.asOver 𝕊 ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊 :=
  lift (toUnit _ ≫ a) (𝟙 _) ≫ μ

blocks.docstring:
A *special subvariety* of the semiabelian variety `X`: the translate $a \cdot H$ of an
irreducible algebraic subgroup `H` of `X` by a torsion point `a`.

justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.IsSpecialSubvariety
justification.why_needed: Special subvarieties of a semiabelian variety: translates of irreducible algebraic subgroups by torsion points (as in the Wikipedia article).

blocks.name: IsSpecialSubvariety
blocks.text:
/-- A *special subvariety* of the semiabelian variety `X`: the translate $a \cdot H$ of an
irreducible algebraic subgroup `H` of `X` by a torsion point `a`. -/
def IsSpecialSubvariety (T : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H ∧ IsIrreducible H ∧
    ∃ a : Points X, IsOfFinOrder a ∧ T = (translation X a).left.base '' H

blocks.code:
def IsAtypicalSubvariety (V Z : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set X, IsSpecialSubvariety X T ∧
    Maximal (fun W => IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z ∧
    topologicalKrullDim V + topologicalKrullDim T <
      topologicalKrullDim Z + topologicalKrullDim X
blocks.docstring:
`Z` is an *atypical subvariety* of `V`: an irreducible component of $V \cap T$ for some
special subvariety `T` of `X`, with $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$, i.e.
$\dim V + \dim T < \dim Z + \dim X$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `irreducibleComponents` (only for whole spaces, so `Maximal` on subsets was used) and `topologicalKrullDim` for dimension.
justification.name: ZilberPinkConjecture.IsAtypicalSubvariety
justification.why_needed: Atypical subvarieties of V: irreducible components Z of V ∩ T (T special) with dim Z > dim V + dim T − dim X, written as dim V + dim T < dim Z + dim X in WithBot ℕ∞ using `topologicalKrullDim`; irreducible component expressed as `Maximal (fun W => IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z`.

blocks.name: IsAtypicalSubvariety
blocks.text:
/-- `Z` is an *atypical subvariety* of `V`: an irreducible component of $V \cap T$ for some
special subvariety `T` of `X`, with $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$, i.e.
$\dim V + \dim T < \dim Z + \dim X$. -/
def IsAtypicalSubvariety (V Z : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set X, IsSpecialSubvariety X T ∧
    Maximal (fun W => IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z ∧
    topologicalKrullDim V + topologicalKrullDim T <
      topologicalKrullDim Z + topologicalKrullDim X

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem comp_translation (a y : Points X) : (y ≫ translation X a : Points X) = a * y := by
  simp only [translation, Hom.mul_def, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
  congr 2
  simp
blocks.docstring:
Composing a $\mathbb{C}$-point `y` with the translation by `a` gives the product `a * y`
in the group $X(\mathbb{C})$.
blocks.name: comp_translation
blocks.text:
/-- Composing a $\mathbb{C}$-point `y` with the translation by `a` gives the product `a * y`
in the group $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem comp_translation (a y : Points X) : (y ≫ translation X a : Points X) = a * y := by
  simp only [translation, Hom.mul_def, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
  congr 2
  simp

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem translation_one : translation X 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
  change (toUnit _ ≫ (1 : Points X)) * 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _
  rw [Hom.one_def, ← Category.assoc, toUnit_unique (toUnit _ ≫ toUnit _) (toUnit _),
    ← Hom.one_def, one_mul]
blocks.docstring: Translation by the identity is the identity.
blocks.name: translation_one
blocks.text:
/-- Translation by the identity is the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem translation_one : translation X 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
  change (toUnit _ ≫ (1 : Points X)) * 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _
  rw [Hom.one_def, ← Category.assoc, toUnit_unique (toUnit _ ≫ toUnit _) (toUnit _),
    ← Hom.one_def, one_mul]

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ : IsAlgebraicSubgroup X Set.univ :=
  ⟨isClosed_univ, ⊤, by simp⟩
blocks.docstring: The whole of `X` is an algebraic subgroup of `X`.
blocks.name: isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ
blocks.text:
/-- The whole of `X` is an algebraic subgroup of `X`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ : IsAlgebraicSubgroup X Set.univ :=
  ⟨isClosed_univ, ⊤, by simp⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isSpecialSubvariety_univ [IrreducibleSpace X] : IsSpecialSubvariety X Set.univ :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ X, IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ X, 1,
    IsOfFinOrder.one, by simp [translation_one]⟩
blocks.docstring: An irreducible group scheme `X` over $\mathbb{C}$ is a special subvariety of itself.
blocks.name: isSpecialSubvariety_univ
blocks.text:
/-- An irreducible group scheme `X` over $\mathbb{C}$ is a special subvariety of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isSpecialSubvariety_univ [IrreducibleSpace X] : IsSpecialSubvariety X Set.univ :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ X, IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ X, 1,
    IsOfFinOrder.one, by simp [translation_one]⟩

blocks.docstring:
**Zilber–Pink conjecture**, semiabelian case (Zilber; Bombieri–Masser–Zannier).

Let $X$ be a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $V \subseteq X$ be a
subvariety (an irreducible Zariski-closed subset). Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal
atypical subvarieties. Here an atypical subvariety of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of
$V \cap T$, where $T \subseteq X$ is a special subvariety (a translate of an irreducible algebraic
subgroup of $X$ by a torsion point), such that $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$; maximality
is with respect to inclusion among the atypical subvarieties of $V$.

claims.decomposer_note: Mixed-Shimura case (Pink's conjecture): for X a mixed Shimura variety over C and V ⊆ X a (closed, algebraic) subvariety, the set of maximal (under inclusion) atypical subvarieties of V is finite, where an atypical subvariety is an irreducible component Z of V ∩ T, T ⊆ X special, with dim Z > dim V + dim T − dim X (dimensions measured in X); equivalently the union of all atypical subvarieties lies in a finite union of proper special subvarieties; implies André–Oort.
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted. All eight candidates (including the two that wrote files) bailed on this slot, and I agree: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib contain no (mixed) Shimura data/varieties, Hermitian symmetric domains, or special subvarieties, and there is no equivalent characterization expressible with existing primitives. Any 'IsMixedShimuraVariety' wrapper with a user-supplied family of special subsets would state a different (vastly over-general) claim.

claims.text_span: if $X$ is a mixed Shimura variety or semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and $V \subseteq X$ is a subvariety, then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties

claims.decomposer_note: Semiabelian case (Zilber's CIT / Bombieri–Masser–Zannier; not a special case of the Shimura version per the article): same finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties, with special subvarieties being torsion translates of irreducible algebraic subgroups (Pink's variant intersects with all algebraic subgroups/cosets—the two formulations are equivalent for the finiteness claim); implies Manin–Mumford and Mordell–Lang.
claims.reviewer_why: c06 and c03 both state the semiabelian case faithfully with the same architecture (group scheme over Spec ℂ via GrpObj in Over (Spec ℂ); algebraic subgroup = closed subset whose ℂ-points form a subgroup; special = torsion translate of an irreducible algebraic subgroup via the translation morphism; atypical = ⊆-maximal irreducible subset of V ∩ T with dim V + dim T < dim Z + dim X in WithBot ℕ∞; conclusion = finiteness of ⊆-maximal atypical subvarieties; V closed irreducible). Both bespoke 'semiabelian' characterizations are provably equivalent to 'connected commutative algebraic group that is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus' (Chevalley + char-0 structure of commutative linear groups): c06 uses 'every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup has a nontrivial torsion point' (𝔾ₐ(ℂ) torsion-free vs. nontrivial connected subgroups of semiabelian varieties are semiabelian with torsion); c03 uses 'every ℂ-morphism 𝔸¹ → G is constant' (also correct). I chose c06 because its `Points` abbreviation and `comp_translation` lemma make the ℂ-points/group semantics explicit and its criterion stays within the file's own vocabulary (no affine-space machinery). Edits: ported c03's `translation_one` API lemma and an `isSpecialSubvariety_univ` test (adapted to c06's definitions), wrapped over-long lines. Compiles with only the `sorry` warning.

context: In mathematics, the Zilber–Pink conjecture is a far-reaching generalisation of many famous Diophantine conjectures and statements, such as André–Oort, Manin–Mumford, and Mordell–Lang. For algebraic tori and semiabelian varieties it was proposed by Boris Zilber and independently by Enrico Bombieri, David Masser, Umberto Zannier in the early 2000's. For semiabelian varieties the conjecture implies the Mordell–Lang and Manin–Mumford conjectures. Richard Pink proposed (again independently) a more general conjecture for Shimura varieties which also implies the André–Oort conjecture. In the case of algebraic tori, Zilber called it the Conjecture on Intersections with Tori (CIT). The general version is now known as the Zilber–Pink conjecture. It states roughly that atypical or unlikely intersections of an algebraic variety with certain special varieties are accounted for by finitely many special varieties.

/-!

Let $X$ be a mixed Shimura variety or a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and let
$V \subseteq X$ be a subvariety. Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal atypical
subvarieties.

Here an *atypical subvariety* of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of an intersection
$V \cap T$, where $T \subseteq X$ is a special subvariety, such that

extension to semiabelian varieties, independently proposed by Bombieri, Masser and Zannier).
The special subvarieties of a semiabelian variety are the translates of irreducible algebraic
subgroups by torsion points.

The mixed Shimura case (Pink's conjecture) is not stated: mixed Shimura varieties and their
special subvarieties are not available in Mathlib.

-/

morphism. Since `X` is a group scheme, this is a group (the group $X(\mathbb{C})$). -/
abbrev Points := 𝟙_ (Over 𝕊) ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊

/-- The point of the underlying space of `X` corresponding to a $\mathbb{C}$-point. -/
def Points.toPoint (x : Points X) : X := x.left.base (default : 𝕊)

/-- An *algebraic subgroup* of `X`: a Zariski-closed subset `H` of `X` whose
$\mathbb{C}$-points form a subgroup of $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Set X) : Prop :=
  IsClosed H ∧ ∃ K : Subgroup (Points X), ∀ x : Points X, x ∈ K ↔ x.toPoint ∈ H

/-- `X` is a *semiabelian variety* over $\mathbb{C}$: a connected commutative algebraic group
over $\mathbb{C}$ (a commutative group scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{C}$
with irreducible underlying space) that is an extension of an abelian variety by an algebraic
torus.

By Chevalley's structure theorem, a connected commutative algebraic group $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$
has a largest connected affine algebraic subgroup $L \cong \mathbb{G}_m^r \times \mathbb{G}_a^s$,
with $X / L$ an abelian variety; $X$ is semiabelian if and only if $s = 0$, i.e. if and only if
$X$ contains no algebraic subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$. Since $\mathbb{G}_a(\mathbb{C})$
is torsion-free, while every nontrivial connected algebraic subgroup of a semiabelian variety is
semiabelian and hence has nontrivial torsion, this is equivalent to the condition used here:
every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of $X$ contains a nontrivial torsion point. -/
structure IsSemiabelianVariety : Prop where
  /-- `X` is locally of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ 𝕊)
  /-- `X` is quasi-compact; together with the previous field, `X` is of finite type over
  $\mathbb{C}$. -/
  compactSpace : CompactSpace X
  /-- `X` is connected (equivalently, irreducible). -/
  irreducibleSpace : IrreducibleSpace X
  /-- The group law of `X` is commutative. -/
  isCommMonObj : IsCommMonObj (X.asOver 𝕊)
  /-- Every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup of `X` contains a nontrivial torsion
  point. -/
  exists_isOfFinOrder : ∀ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H → IsIrreducible H →
    (∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H) →
    ∃ x : Points X, x ≠ 1 ∧ IsOfFinOrder x ∧ x.toPoint ∈ H

/-- Translation $y \mapsto a \cdot y$ by the $\mathbb{C}$-point `a`, as an automorphism of the
$\mathbb{C}$-scheme `X`. -/
noncomputable def translation (a : Points X) : X.asOver 𝕊 ⟶ X.asOver 𝕊 :=
  lift (toUnit _ ≫ a) (𝟙 _) ≫ μ

/-- A *special subvariety* of the semiabelian variety `X`: the translate $a \cdot H$ of an
irreducible algebraic subgroup `H` of `X` by a torsion point `a`. -/
def IsSpecialSubvariety (T : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Set X, IsAlgebraicSubgroup X H ∧ IsIrreducible H ∧
    ∃ a : Points X, IsOfFinOrder a ∧ T = (translation X a).left.base '' H

/-- `Z` is an *atypical subvariety* of `V`: an irreducible component of $V \cap T$ for some
special subvariety `T` of `X`, with $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$, i.e.
$\dim V + \dim T < \dim Z + \dim X$. -/
def IsAtypicalSubvariety (V Z : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set X, IsSpecialSubvariety X T ∧
    Maximal (fun W => IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ V ∩ T) Z ∧
    topologicalKrullDim V + topologicalKrullDim T <
      topologicalKrullDim Z + topologicalKrullDim X

/-- Composing a $\mathbb{C}$-point `y` with the translation by `a` gives the product `a * y`
in the group $X(\mathbb{C})$. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem comp_translation (a y : Points X) : (y ≫ translation X a : Points X) = a * y := by
  simp only [translation, Hom.mul_def, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
  congr 2
  simp

/-- Translation by the identity is the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem translation_one : translation X 1 = 𝟙 _ := by
  change (toUnit _ ≫ (1 : Points X)) * 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _
  rw [Hom.one_def, ← Category.assoc, toUnit_unique (toUnit _ ≫ toUnit _) (toUnit _),
    ← Hom.one_def, one_mul]

/-- The whole of `X` is an algebraic subgroup of `X`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ : IsAlgebraicSubgroup X Set.univ :=
  ⟨isClosed_univ, ⊤, by simp⟩

/-- An irreducible group scheme `X` over $\mathbb{C}$ is a special subvariety of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem isSpecialSubvariety_univ [IrreducibleSpace X] : IsSpecialSubvariety X Set.univ :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isAlgebraicSubgroup_univ X, IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ X, 1,
    IsOfFinOrder.one, by simp [translation_one]⟩

/-- **Zilber–Pink conjecture**, semiabelian case (Zilber; Bombieri–Masser–Zannier).

Let $X$ be a semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $V \subseteq X$ be a
subvariety (an irreducible Zariski-closed subset). Then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal
atypical subvarieties. Here an atypical subvariety of $V$ is an irreducible component $Z$ of
$V \cap T$, where $T \subseteq X$ is a special subvariety (a translate of an irreducible algebraic
subgroup of $X$ by a torsion point), such that $\dim Z > \dim V + \dim T - \dim X$; maximality
is with respect to inclusion among the atypical subvarieties of $V$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem zilber_pink_conjecture.parts.ii (hX : IsSemiabelianVariety X) (V : Set X)
    (hV : IsClosed V) (hV' : IsIrreducible V) :
    {Z : Set X | Maximal (IsAtypicalSubvariety X V) Z}.Finite := by
  sorry

end ZilberPinkConjecture

items: Semiabelian variety is defined by a characterization rather than as an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (neither exists in Mathlib): a connected commutative group scheme of finite type over ℂ in which every nontrivial irreducible algebraic subgroup has a nontrivial torsion point. Justification (Chevalley): the maximal connected affine subgroup is 𝔾_m^r × 𝔾_a^s and X is semiabelian iff s = 0; 𝔾_a(ℂ) is torsion-free, while nontrivial connected algebraic subgroups of semiabelian varieties are semiabelian and have torsion. A reviewer should check this equivalence.

Algebraic groups over ℂ are modeled as group objects `GrpObj (X.asOver (Spec ℂ))` in `Over (Spec ℂ)`; finite type is expressed as `LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec ℂ)` plus `CompactSpace X`; connectedness as `IrreducibleSpace X` (equivalent for group schemes over a field). Separatedness/reducedness are omitted as automatic over ℂ.

Algebraic subgroups are Zariski-closed subsets whose ℂ-points form a subgroup of X(ℂ) (set-level, not scheme-theoretic); over ℂ this coincides with underlying sets of (reduced) closed subgroup schemes, which is what the conjecture concerns.

Special subvarieties are torsion translates a·H of irreducible algebraic subgroups, following the Wikipedia article (rather than Pink's variant with all algebraic subgroups/cosets, which the notes say is equivalent for the finiteness claim). The translate is the image of H under the translation automorphism of X.
'Subvariety' V is taken to be an irreducible Zariski-closed subset of X (standard usage in Pink/Zilber/Bombieri–Masser–Zannier); the version for reducible closed V follows from the irreducible one.

Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions (in `WithBot ℕ∞`) of subsets of the underlying space; the atypicality inequality dim Z > dim V + dim T − dim X is written additively as dim V + dim T < dim Z + dim X, which is equivalent since all four dimensions are finite and non-⊥ (V, T, Z nonempty, X finite type over ℂ).
Irreducible components of V ∩ T are expressed as ⊆-maximal irreducible subsets of V ∩ T; 'maximal atypical subvarieties' are ⊆-maximal elements of the set of atypical subvarieties of V.

Only Points X (the ℂ-points as sections of the structure morphism) are used to define torsion and subgroup properties; closed points of a finite-type ℂ-scheme are exactly images of ℂ-points, so no information is lost.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the source: the list entry does not say whether 'subvariety' means irreducible; the file follows the standard convention (Pink; Habegger–Pila) of irreducible closed subvarieties and documents this. The source does not define 'semiabelian variety'; Mathlib lacks tori and abelian varieties, so the file uses an equivalent characterization (documented in the docstring with its justification) — a reviewer with algebraic-groups background should confirm the equivalence (I verified both directions: Chevalley's theorem gives L ≅ 𝔾ₘʳ × 𝔾ₐˢ for the maximal connected affine subgroup; s > 0 yields a closed irreducible subgroup 𝔾ₐ with no nontrivial torsion; s = 0 means every nontrivial connected subgroup is a nontrivial semiabelian variety and hence has torsion). Reducedness/separatedness of X are omitted as automatic for group schemes of finite type over ℂ. On the six bail-outs for slot (ii): their concern that a theorem-dependent characterization is 'not recognisable as the source definition' is legitimate caution, but the repository accepts documented equivalent characterizations when a primitive is missing (e.g. Wikipedia/ModularityConjecture.lean), and the equivalence here is standard and checked; shipping it is not a 'close enough' compromise but a mathematically equivalent statement. Slot (i) is omitted with certainty: nothing resembling mixed Shimura varieties exists in Mathlib.
statement: Zilber–Pink conjecture that if $X$ is a mixed Shimura variety or semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and $V \subseteq X$ is a subvariety, then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.
